purpose: Allow the Terminal organ to submit human conversation stimuli to an already model-locked JANUS instance and receive a sealed identity-bound response only after the exact model-locked HRAiN organ has produced a verified query-bound memory context from the Meta Registry projection. Human-facing surface semantics are distinct from the proof envelope: an ordinary question must not be replaced by a system-status dump, while an explicit status request may expose the bounded system proof. A recognized bounded integer-choice request is answered directly from a sealed resident/request/turn derivation that does not consume HRAiN memory content, even though the response remains HRAiN-context-bound for provenance. A query-bound context may legitimately contain zero selected memories when HRAiN explicitly proves no forced fill semantics; that empty retrieval is neither HRAiN failure nor negative evidence. A separately sealed and cryptographically bound Terminal cancellation tombstone may suppress future cognition for its exact request without deleting request or response provenance.
proof_rule: A Terminal response proves only that a specific persistent JANUS identity instantiated a specific exact model/file-fabric version, routed the bound request through the exact model-locked HRAiN organ, bound an integrity-verified query-specific HRAiN memory context and its Meta Registry source commit, and processed the request under the read-only conversation authority ceiling. Human-facing response surface is separately classified: a direct bounded integer choice may be cryptographically derived from the sealed request/resident/turn binding without using HRAiN memory content, and an explicit system-status request may expose the bounded status proof. A zero-memory context proves only that this exact HRAiN retrieval selected no strong relevant memory under its explicit no-forced-fill policy; it does not prove absence in the world, negative evidence, or HRAiN failure. A verified cancellation proves only that an admitted Terminal actor cancelled future cognition for one exact sealed request identified by message ID/hash; it neither deletes the request/response nor grants command, claim, truth, proof, or effect authority. Retrieved memory claims are not thereby scientifically true and no command or effect is authorized.
